title: Static table versus interactive grid
summary: Use a semantic table for primarily read-only tabular information and a managed grid only when cell-level interaction or directional navigation materially benefits the task.
problem: Turning every data table into a grid creates complex keyboard behavior, while static tables become inefficient when users need spreadsheet-like interaction.
use_when: Choosing how to represent structured rows and columns
A data surface may include selection, editing, or dense cell interaction
avoid_when: The information is not genuinely tabular
rationale: Table and grid have different keyboard and focus models.
Native table semantics are simpler when cell-level interaction is unnecessary.

use_if: Choosing how to represent structured rows and columns
A data surface may include selection, editing, or dense cell interaction
prefer_alternatives_if: Cards or lists better reflect non-tabular content relationships

requirements: Use native table semantics when possible for static data.
If implementing a grid, provide managed keyboard navigation and a clear focus model.
Keep headers associated with data cells.
keyboard: A grid needs directional navigation; a static table does not turn every cell into a managed focus target.

requirements: Decide interaction model before choosing roles.
Do not use grid solely for visual styling.
Keep row and column relationships perceivable at responsive widths.
